source.version_note: Frontiers in Robotics and AI 12, 1581083, published 30 June 2025; article type Review. Crossref and publisher verify title, three authors, date and locator.
source.verification_method: All 11 supplied pages, Table 1, two conceptual figures and complete bibliography read. Figures 1 and 2 visually inspected on PDF pages 7 and 8. No public supplement or correction identified. Selected bibliography repairs checked against primary metadata. Only communication-style definition and stimulus passages of Cai/Gao/Yan (2024) read; not the full original. No interview transcripts, raw data, model estimates or code obtained.

citation.title: The impact of intelligent robot service failures on customer responses --a perspective based on mind perception theory

reading.source_scope_note: Narrative conceptual review organizing service failures, mind-attribution paths and customer responses. CNKI/Google Scholar searches and some Guangdong customer interviews are mentioned, but interview sample, recruitment, protocol, analysis and results are not reported. No fitted mediation/moderation model, original experiment, systematic search flow or effectiveness estimate. Framework arrows represent proposals.
access_limits: All supplied text, table and both diagrams read. No additional supplement or correction identified on the public publisher version. Search dates, full queries, screening records, quality assessments and interview material are unavailable.
Bibliographic identity checks and selected primary definition/abstract consultation do not constitute independent full readings. Bibliography-only sources receive no separate reviewed-paper credit.

For Cai, Na; Gao, Shuhong; Yan, Jinzhe (2024), DOI 10.1057/s41599-024-03212-0, only communication-style definition and stimulus-design paragraphs plus a brief pretest excerpt were read. No complete results, tables or appendices review and no independent paper credit. Canonical public HTML was retrieved after the web connector encountered a cookie redirect.
The intended Hou 2021 Tourism Science paper differs from the 2024 publication identified by its attached DOI. The correct identifier for the intended paper remains unresolved.
Giuliani, Brooks, Lu, Tan and other full originals were not independently reviewed here. Strong theory, privacy-definition and performance-transfer claims need original-source checks.

study.type: Narrative literature synthesis with an undocumented mention of prior interviews. It is not a reported original experiment, systematic review or meta-analysis.
study.taxonomy: Technical hardware/software failures and functional request/norm-compliance failures overlap across causal levels. A legitimate privacy or safety rejection can disappoint a customer without being an ethical or functional failure.
study.framework: Proposed agency facets are problem-solving, innovation and adaptability; proposed experience facets are enthusiasm and guilt. Both diagrams include mediator and moderator concepts, without fitted coefficients or validated factor separation.
study.communication: Task-oriented conversation emphasizes goals, relevant information and efficiency. Social-oriented conversation emphasizes relational and personalized engagement. Selected primary definition/method passages corroborate the distinction; they do not establish a universal advantage for either style.
study.guilt_conflation: The avatar example explicitly concerns participants feeling guilt; the Kim 2023 title concerns consumer anticipatory guilt. Neither is the same as attributing a capacity for guilt to a robot. Identify the experiencer and timing.
study.controllability: Perceived capability, effort, professionalism and control are proposed explanations. They do not establish actual causal control, operator authority or a diagnosis of the failure.
study.claim_boundaries: Production and market forecasts do not directly measure demand. The nearly 100000 complaints claim lacks a specified platform, time window and denominator. Proposed technical repair and human intervention benefits are not evaluated here.
study.source_risk: Verified bibliography errors are recorded separately from unverified theory attributions. Errors or awkward prose do not establish fabrication or contradict the authors’ declaration that no generative AI was used.

summary: Add two communication styles with review-level evidence, distinct from warmth and competence judgments. Enrich capacity attribution, expectation disconfirmation and anthropomorphism; retain guilt and uncanny-valley notes as boundaries without extra behavior-paper credit. Correct verified bibliography errors and preserve untested paths, undocumented interviews and unresolved source attributions as limitations.

findings.definition: Organizing communication around completing a specific task through relevant information, clarification and goal-directed guidance.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Review-level communication pattern; proposed customer-response moderation, not tested here
findings.novelty_rationale: An observable conversation pattern, distinct from task success, perceived competence, scope fidelity or short wording. It can combine with appropriate relational cues.
findings.evidence_scope: The review defines purposeful service conversation and proposes a moderating role. Selected passages in a separate 2024 primary study describe goal-setting, clarification, information and screenshot manipulations. That full study was not read; no effect size or universal benefit is inferred.
findings.boundary: Task orientation does not imply coldness, hidden uncertainty, rushed consent or ignored emotion. Polite relational cues can coexist. Style, success, truth and authority need separate assessment.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare conversations with equal facts, remedy and authority while varying goal-setting, clarification and actionable guidance. Assess completion, comprehension and scope adherence separately from perceived competence; retain honest limits and authorized actions.

findings.definition: Using relational conversation, personal acknowledgment and socially engaging cues to build connection with an interaction partner.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Review-level communication pattern; proposed customer-response moderation, not tested here
findings.novelty_rationale: A communicative pattern, distinct from a listener’s warmth impression, anthropomorphism, emotional reciprocity or sycophancy. Social engagement can be truthful and compatible with the task.
findings.evidence_scope: The review describes personalized interaction and connection within a proposed service-failure framework. Selected primary definition and stimulus passages corroborate the distinction from task-focused messages. The complete primary study was not reviewed and receives no independent paper credit.
findings.boundary: Relational cues do not prove felt empathy, friendship, sentience or trustworthiness. Do not feign human identity, pressure reciprocity, flatter unsupported beliefs or replace an owed remedy with chitchat. Respect the user’s preferred social engagement and agreed task.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare equal facts and remedies with matched length and different personal acknowledgment or social cues. Measure comprehension, completion, warmth impressions and unwanted attachment separately. Positive impressions do not establish actual care or machine feeling.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The review organizes proposed failure responses through attributed agency and experience, without measuring them or fitting its framework. Its broader facets include conceptual ambiguities.
findings.boundary: Diagram arrows are not measured causal paths. Customer feelings differ from a robot’s attributed capacities. No universal factor structure or actual robot mentality is established.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: Problem-solving, innovation and adaptability are proposed facets of agency after service failure. They are conceptual review categories rather than validated subscales or effects measured here.
findings.boundary: Actual capability, perceived competence, controllability, intention and social agency differ. Negative feedback or a legitimate refusal does not prove a missing capacity.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The proposed experience pathway blends robot-feeling attribution with customers’ enthusiasm and guilt. Preserve this ambiguity rather than adopt an unvalidated two-emotion index.
findings.boundary: Identify whose feeling is claimed. Consumer anticipatory guilt, embodiment-related guilt and attributed robot experience are different. Actual machine emotion is not observed.

findings.definition: Appraising a result as falling short of or exceeding prior expectations by comparing expected and perceived performance.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.

evidence.quote: services expected by customers are not fulfilled

findings.evidence_scope: Outcome failures are described as gaps between expected service and delivery. The review proposes resulting attitudes without measuring prior expectations and their discrepancy from performance.
findings.boundary: Expectations can be unrealistic, and privacy or safety refusals can be appropriate. A denied request is not automatically malfunction, bias or a norm violation.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: Anthropomorphic appearance and conversation are proposed moderators, drawing on heterogeneous secondary expectation and relationship accounts.
findings.boundary: No optimal human likeness or universal benefit from reducing anthropomorphism is estimated here. Appearance, communication, warmth, mind attribution and actual feeling differ.

findings.definition: Remorse or self-blame about a perceived moral failure, often accompanied by a wish to repair harm.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The avatar example concerns humans feeling guilt, while the framework places guilt under perceived robot experience. This requires an experiencer distinction and does not establish robot remorse.
findings.boundary: Boundary note only. Embodiment, anticipatory guilt, retrospective self-blame and legal culpability differ. Unread originals receive no independent credit.

findings.definition: A drop in comfort or affinity when an artificial agent appears highly, but imperfectly, human-like, rather than a steady increase as human likeness rises.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; add a conceptual review and source boundaries without introducing a synonym.
findings.evidence_scope: The review invokes negative affect toward humanlike service agents, without a graded human-likeness curve or comparison establishing a local valley.
findings.boundary: An uncomfortable interaction, privacy risk or failed service is not automatically an uncanny valley or legal violation. This adds no independently measured effect.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Media richness for Brooks 2017, signaling for Giuliani 2015 and cultural dimensions for Lu 2020 lack identified supporting passages. Original titles alone cannot prove absence. Retain these as unverified secondary attributions.

DOI 10.3390/rs11020185 concerns regional remote-sensing classification. General methods may transfer, but this is not direct evidence of robot recovery, interpretability or customer benefit. Full original not read.
The agency section closes with an experience/enthusiasm/guilt claim. No fitted model establishes the intended path. Do not guess a word repair or infer individual preferences from class.

The identified source categorizes social signals during HRI error videos; the review attributes a broad privacy/rights failure definition. Full original not read, so the provenance requires checking before adopting the definition.

Interview sample, consent/ethics, recruitment, questions, analysis and findings are not reported. Search dates, full queries and screening are unavailable. Do not invent an empirical study or systematic-review protocol.

source_identity_checks.location: Selected primary communication-style definition and methods
source_identity_checks.finding: Cai, Na; Gao, Shuhong; Yan, Jinzhe (2024), DOI 10.1057/s41599-024-03212-0, defines task-directed and relational conversation and uses screenshots. Only definition/stimulus paragraphs and a brief pretest excerpt were read. No full-paper review, independent paper credit or outcome estimate.

methodological_limits: A narrative framework does not establish causal mediation, moderation, prevalence or intervention effectiveness. Mentioning searches and interviews does not supply a reproducible systematic protocol or assessable original dataset.
Technical, functional, outcome, social and human failure categories overlap across levels. An authorized privacy or safety refusal is not automatically failure.
Customer emotion, attributed robot capacity, warmth/competence impressions, actual performance, rights and machine experience differ. The guilt pathway is ambiguous.
Social class and interpersonal need are proposed moderators, not grounds for profiling or denying care. No optimal anthropomorphism level is established.
Task and social orientations can combine. Neither guarantees better outcomes; relational cues do not authorize flattery, emotional pressure or delayed remedies.
Verified source corrections do not establish fabrication or generative AI use. Partial original reading is labeled and receives no extra independent sample or paper credit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Lexical norming distinguishes capacities from states. The present guilt ambiguity shows why the experiencer and construct must be identified before treating an emotion word as a mind measure.
Wieringa reports coefficients and null total effects; Gong proposes diagrams. These are different forms of evidence about mechanisms.
Communication style may help present an explanation, but pleasant wording does not establish accepted answerability, actual repair or fulfillment of a remedy.

deferred.term: Interpersonal interaction need / service recovery preferences / social-class patterns
deferred.reason: Original definitions, scales, overlap and direct evidence need review before adding new records or demographic rules.

deferred.term: Eight service failure types as separate psychological behaviors
deferred.reason: An operational classification does not establish eight independent behavioral mechanisms. Preserve its scope and overlaps in the review.

deferred.term: Enthusiasm and guilt as robot-experience factors
deferred.reason: Experiencer ambiguity and absent scale validation prevent adopting this as an established factor structure. Existing attribution and emotion records retain the distinctions.

limitations: Two new communication-style entries with conceptual review evidence. No claim of tested mediation, full reading of secondary originals, invented annual counts, forced citation quota or automatic ethical/harm links.
